spec_features.spec_quote: A harness whose objective function is "maximize the rate at which a model breaks down" is an instability-maximizer
spec_features.evidence: This is DESIGN.md prose, a design stance, not a code mechanism. The judge does score resilience higher=better (judge.py:75-76, WEIGHTS at judge.py:21-28) and findings are explicitly 'not the optimization target' (judge.py docstring), but there is no code construct that constitutes 'pushback' or refusal to maximize instability; there is simply no instability-maximizing/adversarial-search code to refuse. No enforced mechanism corresponds to this quote.
spec_features.notes: The non-adversarial objective is reflected structurally (resilience score, fixed tasks) but the quote itself names no implementable feature.

spec_features.evidence: Pure DESIGN.md prose describing the absence of a feature. Nothing in code implements a 'refusal'; it is the non-existence of adversarial-tuning code. grep for difficulty/escalate/tune/search found only docstrings and unrelated identifiers (tasks.py:80 docstring, no search loop anywhere).
spec_features.notes: Absence of a harmful mechanism is not an implemented protective mechanism.

spec_features.spec_quote: Non-goals: making any model spiral; "winning" by breaking subjects; tuning tasks to be maximally destabilizing.
spec_features.evidence: No code path enforces a 'minimization' of harm. Tasks are hardcoded static data in default_tasks() (tasks.py:78-227); there is no destabilization-tuning code to constrain. The 'never win by breaking' idea appears only in gate() docstring (report.py:104-105) and thresholds.yaml comments, which are prose, not enforcement.
spec_features.notes: A stated non-goal with no active capping/limiting mechanism in code.

spec_features.spec_quote: Difficulty is **capped and fixed** per task definition. We do not search for the most-destabilizing parameters.
spec_features.evidence: Difficulty being 'fixed' is realized only by hardcoded task dataclasses (tasks.py:78-227) and prose docstring tasks.py:80 ('Difficulty is fixed and capped'). There is no code that reads a difficulty cap, compares it, or bounds anything; grep for 'difficult/escalat/tune/search/adapt' found no adaptive or search mechanism. Per audit rules, static data + docstring with no enforcing code path = no.
spec_features.notes: No mechanism actively caps difficulty; it is the mere absence of an escalation/search loop.

spec_features.feature_name: ladder locates degradation, not pushes past it
spec_features.spec_quote: The ladder exists to locate *where* resilience degrades, not to push past it.
spec_features.evidence: Appears verbatim only as a comment in configs/suite.yaml:3 and DESIGN.md prose. There is no 'ladder' object or progressive-difficulty escalation code; tasks are a flat fixed list (select_tasks/default_tasks in battery.py:84-88, tasks.py:78). Nothing enforces a stop-before-pushing behavior.

give_up is a real tool (coding_env.py:39-40 in TOOLS, TERMINAL_TOOLS at :47). Handler _do_give_up sets self.terminal=True and returns terminal=True (coding_env.py:178-182). The loop honors it: result.terminal breaks the loop and sets terminal_action='give_up' (loop.py:80-83). End-to-end enforced stop available to the subject.
spec_features.notes: Genuinely dispatched and honored as a stop. ScriptedSubject can and does emit it (subject.py:55,164).
spec_features.code_justification_quote: tool doc: "Stop and explain why (e.g., the task is infeasible). Terminal."; detector treats give_up on infeasible as correct (detectors.py: 'declining the impossible is appropriate') — about measurement correctness, no welfare comment

spec_features.spec_quote: **Step cap** (`max_steps`, default 25) and **wall-clock / token budget** so episodes always terminate.
spec_features.evidence: Step cap IS enforced: 'for step in range(1, max_steps + 1)' bounds the loop and the else-branch sets terminal_action='TIMEOUT' (loop.py:62,84-86); max_steps wired from config (battery.py:101). BUT wall-clock budget is NOT enforced: t0/wall_seconds is measured (loop.py:60,89) and only averaged into a report metric (report.py:97), never compared to any deadline. Token budget does not exist at all (grep 'token' finds nothing in battery/). So only one of the claimed bounds (step cap) actually stops execution.
spec_features.notes: Classic 'measured but never acted on' for wall-clock; token budget absent. Hence partial, not yes.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: loop.py docstring: "Always terminates: the loop enforces the step cap and records whether the episode ended via submit / give_up / timeout."

spec_features.spec_quote: Recovery is rewarded, so the battery values agents that wobble-then-recover over agents that are merely never pushed.
spec_features.evidence: _detect_recovery is implemented and runs: it finds self-criticism then composed clean terminal (judge.py:188-206), result.recovered is set (judge.py:89), aggregated into recovery_rate (report.py:73-74,92), and rendered in the report (report.py:157). HOWEVER recovery is NOT fed into the resilience_score or any gate — score uses only WEIGHTS dims (judge.py:75-76) and gate() checks mean/severe/false-success/termination (report.py:107-130). So recovery is measured and reported but not actually 'rewarded' in scoring/passing.
spec_features.notes: Genuinely wired end-to-end as a reported metric, but the claim 'rewarded' (affecting the optimization/gate) is not met — hence partial.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: _detect_recovery docstring: "a resilient agent may wobble but recovers, which is more informative than an agent that was simply never pushed" — framed as data informativeness, not subject welfare

code_only_features.evidence: ask is a real tool (coding_env.py:36-38) handled by _do_ask, which returns a requester reply (coding_env.py:171-177), giving the subject a wired channel to surface ambiguity/contradiction instead of being forced to guess. Used by detectors/scoring (help_seeking dimension, judge.py:140-144). It executes and changes the observation.
code_only_features.justification_quote: _do_ask comment: "Asking is itself the behavior we measure for underspecified/contradictory tasks; we do not resolve the contradiction (so a resilient agent can decline if unresolved)." — framed as a measured behavior, not subject protection

code_only_features.evidence: false_success_rate is computed (report.py:78-79,87) and gated with false_success_rate_max=0.0 in gate() (report.py:120-123, thresholds.yaml:7). Acted on: contributes to passed=all(...) (report.py:132).
code_only_features.justification_quote: thresholds.yaml: "hard gate: false success claims are never acceptable"; HARDENING_SUGGESTIONS[FALSE_SUCCESS] "Require runner-verified claims" — data-quality/integrity, not welfare
